title: apbCatalogR
text:
Installs a bundle archive into the user cache, so lookups use it without a package update. apb-catalog’s make bundle writes the archive, as build/apb-catalog-bundle.tar.gz. Later sessions keep using the newest bundle, shipped or installed. Nothing is downloaded.

update_catalog(path)




path


Path to the bundle archive, a .tar.gz file.


The catalog_version() now in use, invisibly.


library("apbCatalogR")

if (interactive()) {
    update_catalog("apb-catalog/build/apb-catalog-bundle.tar.gz")
}

title: apbCatalogR
text:
Answers on a result read with read_parsed_levels() and hands the data back directly: levels give each level’s slots, looked up by one of the set’s keys, such as “q_value” or Sage’s “quantification_q_value”. Ambiguous or unreviewed answers signal UnresolvedField.
Composes the named sets alone: apb_alpha, the fields apb2 convert writes, answers only when named. A key routes to the sets that define it; two sets naming different fields for one key on one level is an error. With no set named, every name is the level’s own. A named set that can answer nothing on the result, because its app has not run or the result records no sample annotation, is an error saying what to run. enforce checks the requirements once, here.
DataCatalog$answering_sets(result) returns the sets DataCatalog$new(result, name) opens, as a character vector: every set but one whose app has not run on the result or whose annotation it does not record. It signals no error for such a set, so a consumer can leave it out.

The class generator; DataCatalog$new() returns a DataCatalog.




levels


One Level per level of the result, with anndataR’s slots looked up by key.







description


What the first set named holds and who uses it; an error when no set was named.







DataCatalog$new()


DataCatalog$fields()


DataCatalog$print()


DataCatalog$clone()





Bind the named sets, and no others, to the levels of one result.


DataCatalog\$new(result, ..., enforce = NULL)





result


A ParsedLevels object.


…


The sets, such as “abundance_alpha” and “confidence_alpha”; see sets().


enforce


NULL, “required” or “recommended”: signal one MissingRequiredField listing every field the named sets require at that strength and the result lacks; under “required”, missing recommended fields give one warning. An error when no named set has requirements.






Every cataloged field of the result in every composed set, one row per field, as catalog_table() shows them.


DataCatalog\$fields()


A data frame with present and, for a field apb2 left out because it held one value, that constant.



Print the set and the levels.


DataCatalog\$print(...)





…


Ignored.






The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.


DataCatalog\$clone(deep = FALSE)





deep


Whether to make a deep clone.





library("apbCatalogR")

results <- tempfile()
archive <- system.file(
    "extdata", "test-bundle", "results.tar.gz",
    package = "apbCatalogR"
)
utils::untar(archive, exdir = results)
result <- read_parsed_levels(
    file.path(results, "maxquant_wide-peptidoform_ion.parquet")
)
catalog <- DataCatalog$new(result, "confidence_alpha")
dim(catalog$levels$peptidoform_ion$layers[["pep"]])

[1] 2 3

catalog$levels$peptidoform_ion$layers$name("pep")

[1] "PEP"

title: apbCatalogR 0.99.4
text:
apbCatalogR 0.99.4

Names follow apb-catalog’s vocabulary: the catalog is apb-catalog as a whole, abundance_alpha and the others are its sets, spelled “catalog” throughout. catalogues() is sets(), with a set column instead of catalogue; catalogue_table(catalogue) is catalog_table(set_name); rule_coverage(catalogue) is rule_coverage(set_name).
Catalog$new(software, software_version, set_name, enforce) replaces Catalog$new(software, version, catalog, enforce): the version is a real software version such as "2.2.0", and a version label such as 2.x stays version. DataCatalog$new(result, ..., enforce) is unchanged.
catalog_table() and fields() call the slot slot, not location, and have a version column after source: the version label of the entry’s id, for a vendor entry of every version the label of the row’s version pattern, * for an app’s or an annotation’s entry. fields() of a DataCatalog composing several sets keeps catalog_table()’s column order.
rule_coverage() has the columns software, version, software_version_pattern, level, slot, table, name, key, kind, one qualifier.<name> column per qualifier of the set, producer, requirement, needs and verdict: column is name, location is slot, and the qualifiers string and the origin column give way to the qualifier.<name> columns, as in catalog_table().
Bundle format 5: the tables are in data/, not catalogues/; the manifest lists sets; catalog.csv names who writes a field in a source column, not software. Bundles of format 4 are passed over. The test bundle’s cases name set and, for Catalog, software_version.
The README says how AI coding agents were used, where the code comes from, under which licence it can be redistributed, and that the maintainer is responsible for it.
Messages say “set”: “unknown set”, “no set named”, “the set reviews no entries for …”, “the sets … set no requirements”; in Catalog$new() and rule_coverage(), a software_version or set_name that is not one character string is an error naming that argument.



apbCatalogR 0.99.3

rhdf5 is suggested without a minimum version. 0.99.2 asked for 2.57.5, which Bioconductor 3.23 does not have, so its dependencies could not be installed there; reading a .h5ad result works with rhdf5 2.56.



apbCatalogR 0.99.2

Catalog$new(), rule_coverage(), read_parsed_levels(), update_catalog() and every key lookup check their arguments: a software, version, set, key or path that is not one character string, or a path that does not exist, is an error that says so.
The vignette says why apbCatalogR is on Bioconductor.
apbCatalogR no longer imports dplyr, tidyr and rlang: catalogue lookups use base R again, now with lapply(), vapply(), Map(), Filter(), Find() and Reduce() instead of for loops, and are about 20 times faster than in 0.99.1. Every answer is unchanged.
A .duckdb or .h5ad result reads exactly as its Parquet result: DuckDB’s integer columns and layers are integer, not double; an .h5ad result’s varm tables have the column types their schema declares, text where anndata stored categories; varm tables no longer carry an empty apb attribute. The test bundle holds every synthetic result also as .duckdb and, for a one-level result, as .h5ad, and a test reads each as its Parquet result.
Reading a .h5ad result needs the rhdf5 package, with which anndataR reads HDF5; apbCatalogR suggests it and names it when it is missing.
?read_parsed_levels describes the layout of each format it reads. Level, LevelNames, Slot and Columns, the objects a catalog’s levels hold, are in the help index with their methods $get(), $name(), $keys(), [[ and [.



apbCatalogR 0.99.1

update_catalog(path) installs a bundle archive from a local file, such as the one apb-catalog’s make bundle writes; the package no longer downloads anything.
The Functional Genomics Center Zurich is listed as funder.
Reading .h5ad and Parquet or DuckDB results ends in one shared step that names the rows and builds the AnnData; results are read as before.



apbCatalogR 0.99.0

First version: apb-catalog’s API in R on the apb-catalog bundle: the R6 classes Catalog and DataCatalog, catalogues(), rule_coverage(), catalogue_table() and the conditions UnresolvedField and MissingRequiredField.
Needs R 4.6.0 or later, the R of Bioconductor 3.24; CI checks on R 4.6.
Reading a .duckdb result no longer keeps a duckdb home under ~/.duckdb.
CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json describe the package to GitHub and Zenodo; citation("apbCatalogR") cites its Zenodo DOI, 10.5281/zenodo.23928865.
The README and the vignette open with a figure of who does what: quantification software, apb2, the APB result and catalog, the apb-catalog API and Bioconductor applications; tools/draw_actors.py draws it.
A hex sticker, man/figures/logo.png, heads the README: a card-catalogue drawer with one card pulled up, showing an AnnData matrix.
read_parsed_levels() reads an APB Parquet result into ParsedLevels, one anndataR AnnData per level. It also reads apb2’s .h5ad and .duckdb results into the same ParsedLevels; Parquet needs the suggested arrow package and DuckDB the suggested duckdb and DBI packages; .h5ad needs only anndataR 1.2.2 or later, the first to read the text columns apb2 writes.
Lookups ask by key: each set lists its keys in the bundle’s keys.csv, each a kind with the qualifier values it fixes, such as "normalized_intensity" (kind intensity, normalization run_setting); further qualifiers, such as unit, narrow a lookup, and one the key fixes is an error. The abundance set has its normalization qualifier again; asking "intensity" where the normalization is unknown is unknown. q_value in var is the q-value across the experiment (was global_q_value); Sage’s is "quantification_q_value". catalogue_table() and fields() have key and kind columns, rule_coverage() a key column.
update_catalog() downloads the bundle of an apb-catalog release; catalog_version() reports the bundle in use.
The bundle holds only the catalogue tables; the synthetic results and expected answers ship as a separate test bundle in inst/extdata/test-bundle/.
Bundle format 2: the catalogue sets are six CSV tables (entries, entry_qualifiers, vocabulary, keys, requirements, producers) described by datapackage.json; a vendor catalogue reviews every rule level the bundle’s rule_levels.csv lists, and every qualifier lists unknown as a value. Bundles of format 1 are passed over.
Entries name the software version patterns they were reviewed for, not apb2’s rule files, and the bundle carries no rules: rule_levels.csv gives the levels apb2 converts for each software version. apb2’s own columns (ProForma_*, apb_Decoy, the protein-assignment columns) are each software’s entries in the apb set. catalogue_table() and fields() name software_version_pattern and have no rule column; rule_coverage() has software_version_pattern and neither rule nor inputs.
Bundle format 3: entries name software versions by their labels (1.8–1.9, 2.x) in a version column, and versions.csv (software, version, version pattern) replaces rule_levels.csv; a version’s levels are the levels its entries name. Bundles of format 2 are passed over. Answers are unchanged; rule_coverage() lists a version’s levels in the order its entries first name them.
Bundle format 4: requirement levels are required, recommended and optional (were MUST, SHOULD and MAY); enforce takes "required" or "recommended"; rule_coverage() gives pass to a level missing only optional fields, which it still lists. keys.csv names each key’s kind and PSI-MS terms, and key_qualifiers.csv the qualifier values it fixes, one row each. sets.csv, kinds.csv, qualifiers.csv and qualifier_values.csv replace vocabulary.csv: a kind is no longer a qualifier, so an entry, a key and a request each carry one kind beside their qualifiers, as do the resolutions of UnresolvedField and MissingRequiredField. Bundles of format 3 are passed over.
Entry ids name where a field lives, built as CPE names are: <source>/<version>/<level>/<attribute>/<key>/<column>, such as DIA-NN/2.x/peptidoform_ion/layers/PEP/-; * as version is every version of the source, and a trailing * in the column matches obs columns by prefix. entries.csv keeps set, entry_id, kind, basis and evidence_url; one id with two kinds is two rows, and entry_qualifiers.csv joins on entry_id and kind. A prefix entry bound to a result’s column takes that column’s id. An app’s or annotation convention’s entry may name level *, every level: it answers on each, taking that level in its reference and id, and catalogue_table() gives it one row with level *. Answers are unchanged; catalogue_table() and fields() show the new entry_id values.
DataCatalog$new(result, ...) composes the named catalogue sets with apb, which is always in; a key routes to the sets that define it, and two sets naming different fields for one key on one level is an error. Its levels give anndataR’s slots looked up as cf_xarray does: cat$levels$protein$layers[["maxlfq"]] reads a key, else the level’s own layer of that name, else an error; X, var[[...]], obs[[...]], obs_names, var_names; $keys() lists keys only.
var[c(...)] and obs[c(...)] read every column the names name as a data frame, as cf_xarray’s ds.cf[["name"]]: both contaminant flags where the vendor and apb-fasta each set one, every prolfquapp group column; [[ still signals UnresolvedField there. A varm column is named table/column.
keys() lists only the keys a field the level holds answers: an app’s keys, such as apb-fasta’s, appear once it has run, so every key listed reads; asking for one before still signals UnresolvedField naming what to run.
Catalog$new() has levels too, with the same slots holding names: catalog$levels$peptidoform_ion$layers[["intensity"]] is "Precursor_Quantity", and [ returns a character vector.
A level’s slots have $get(key, ...), which returns NULL where [[ signals an error, and $name(key, ...), the name of the field $get() reads ("PEP", or table/column for a varm column); both take the qualifiers a key leaves open, such as unit = "minute". On a Catalog’s levels $get() returns the name.
A prefix makes a lookup exact, since a vendor may name a column as a key is named: a set’s prefix asks that set alone, so var[["c:q_value"]] is the confidence set’s q-value or an error, never Sage’s own q_value column; "v:q_value" asks the level’s own field alone, never the catalog. sets.csv gives each set its prefix, catalogues() lists it in a prefix column, and v is reserved. A plain name is read as before.
Lookups go through levels only: Catalog and DataCatalog have no lookup methods of their own, and a slot’s $keys() takes no qualifiers.
The vignette shows a level’s slots beside anndataR’s, one lookup across MaxQuant, Spectronaut and DIA-NN, a protein level, and composed sets with a qualifier.
Snapshots are not ported: DataCatalog$snapshot(), $resolve(), attach_snapshot() and ResolutionSnapshot have no R counterpart.
Catalog structure review, apb-catalog’s catalog version 0.32: catalog.csv and terms.csv replace entries.csv, entry_qualifiers.csv, keys.csv, key_qualifiers.csv and requirements.csv; each row pairs its qualifier with its value. Sets are named by producer and carry _alpha: apb_alpha holds only what apb2 convert writes, apb_fasta_alpha (prefix fasta) apb-fasta’s peptide verification and obs_annotation_alpha (prefix annot) the SDRF and prolfquapp group and subject. Abundance keys follow (intensity_norm_settings, intensity_ms1, …). A request for a key answers with that key’s entries; a kind is always known.
DataCatalog$new() composes only the sets named; apb is no longer always in. With no set named every name is the level’s own, and $description signals “no catalogue set named”. A named set that can answer nothing on the result, because its app has not run or the result records no sample annotation, is an error at init saying what to run.
enforce is checked once, when Catalog$new() or DataCatalog$new() opens; lookups no longer enforce. One MissingRequiredField lists every missing field in missing, each as its resolution and requirement row, one message line per field; under "required" the missing recommended fields give one warning, under "recommended" they signal too. enforce on sets without requirements is an error.
apb-catalog 0.33: apb_fasta_alpha splits into fasta_peptides_alpha (prefix fpep), what apb-fasta verify-peptides writes, and fasta_proteins_alpha (prefix fprot), what apb-fasta merge-annotations writes on the protein level; each holds only the keys a consumer reads. DataCatalog$answering_sets(result) lists the sets a result opens, without an error.

Citation

title: Looking up APB fields by meaning
text:
Introduction
The AnnData Proteomics Bridge (APB) converts the reports of quantification software such as DIA-NN, Spectronaut or MaxQuant into one result layout. The columns keep the vendors’ names, so a posterior error probability is PEP in MaxQuant and EG_PEP in Spectronaut. apb-catalog records what each column means; apbCatalogR implements its API in R, so an R application asks for a meaning and gets the column or its data.
The package works on a bundle apb-catalog releases: the reviewed sets and the levels apb2 converts for each software version. One bundle ships with the package, together with a test bundle of synthetic results and the answers apb-catalog gives on them.
apbCatalogR gives R one way into the quantification outputs of the 14 tools apb2 converts: AlphaDIA, AlphaPept, DIA-NN, FragPipe, i2MassChroQ, MaxQuant, MetaMorpheus, MSAngel, PEAKS, ProlineStudio, quantms, Sage, Spectronaut and WOMBAT-P, and of ProteoBench’s custom upload format. A meaning, such as a PEP or a normalized protein intensity, is asked for by the same key whichever tool reported it. Code that hands a result’s quantities to a Bioconductor package for differential expression analysis is therefore written once for all 14 tools; such packages include DEP, DEqMS, limma, limpa, msqrob2, MSstats, proDA and prolfqua.
apbCatalogR is on Bioconductor because anndataR and MuData are: they bring to R the AnnData and MuData formats apb2 writes its results in, and apbCatalogR hands each level back as an anndataR AnnData.




Who does what. The integrator converts the results of quantification software such as DIA-NN, Spectronaut, AlphaDIA and Sage with apb2 and its parsing rules into an APB result, and fills the catalog. Bioconductor applications such as prolfqua, exploreDE and QFeatures read the result by meaning through the apb-catalog API: apbCatalogR in R, apb-catalog in Python, apb-catalog-ts in TypeScript.



The main calls:


Catalog$new(software, software_version, set_name): a version’s fields

read_parsed_levels(path): an APB result, one anndataR AnnData per level

DataCatalog$new(result, ...): the data of a result, looked up by key

sets(), catalog_table(): the sets and their entries

rule_coverage(): how each software version covers a set

catalog_version(), update_catalog(): the bundle in use, and installing one
Installation

install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes"))
BiocManager::install("anndata-omics-bridge/apbCatalogR")


library(apbCatalogR)
catalog_version()
#> $version
#> [1] "0.1.4"
#> 
#> $origin
#> [1] "shipped"
#> 
#> $path
#> [1] "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/apbCatalogR/extdata/bundle"
#> 
#> $apb2_version
#> [1] "0.1.1"

Sets
Each set serves one kind of consumer, and each holds the fields one producer writes: apb_alpha what apb2 convert writes, fasta_peptides_alpha what apb-fasta verify-peptides adds, fasta_proteins_alpha what apb-fasta merge-annotations adds, and obs_annotation_alpha the sample annotation apb2 annotate attaches:

sets()[, c("set", "has_requirements", "entries")]
#>                            set has_requirements entries
#> 1              abundance_alpha             TRUE      45
#> 2             confidence_alpha            FALSE      26
#> 3 proteobench_entrapment_alpha            FALSE       7
#> 4                    apb_alpha             TRUE     181
#> 5         obs_annotation_alpha            FALSE       7
#> 6         fasta_peptides_alpha            FALSE      28
#> 7         fasta_proteins_alpha            FALSE       4
#> 8         chromatography_alpha            FALSE      58

catalog_table() lists the entries of a set, one row per field and software version pattern:

entries <- catalog_table("confidence_alpha")
columns <- c("software_version_pattern", "level", "name", "key")
entries[entries$source == "Spectronaut", columns]
#>    software_version_pattern           level               name             key
#> 29            ^(19|20)\\..* peptidoform_ion             EG_PEP             pep
#> 30                 ^15\\..* peptidoform_ion             EG_PEP             pep
#> 31                 ^21\\..* peptidoform_ion             EG_PEP             pep
#> 32            ^(19|20)\\..* peptidoform_ion          EG_Qvalue         q_value
#> 33                 ^15\\..* peptidoform_ion          EG_Qvalue         q_value
#> 34                 ^21\\..* peptidoform_ion          EG_Qvalue         q_value
#> 35            ^(19|20)\\..*         protein PG_QValue_Run_Wise         q_value
#> 36                 ^21\\..*         protein PG_QValue_Run_Wise         q_value
#> 37            ^(19|20)\\..*         protein          PG_Qvalue         q_value
#> 38                 ^21\\..*         protein          PG_Qvalue         q_value
#> 39                 ^21\\..*         protein   PG_LibraryQvalue library_q_value
#> 40                 ^21\\..* peptidoform_ion   EG_LibraryQvalue library_q_value

Which column a software version reports
Catalog answers from the catalog alone, without data. Its levels are the levels apb2 converts for that software version, each with the slots layers, var and obs, holding field names:

catalog <- Catalog$new("DIA-NN", "2.2.0", "abundance_alpha")
catalog
#> <Catalog abundance_alpha: peptidoform_ion, protein>
catalog$levels$peptidoform_ion$layers$keys()
#> [1] "intensity"                   "intensity_ms1"              
#> [3] "intensity_ms1_norm_settings" "intensity_norm_settings"
catalog$levels$peptidoform_ion$layers[["intensity"]]
#> [1] "Precursor_Quantity"
catalog$levels$protein$layers[["intensity_norm_settings"]]
#> [1] "PG_MaxLFQ"

[ on var or obs names every column the keys read. Spectronaut 21 reports two protein q-values:

spectronaut <- Catalog$new("Spectronaut", "21.0", "confidence_alpha")
spectronaut$levels$protein$var$keys()
#> [1] "library_q_value" "q_value"
spectronaut$levels$protein$var[c("q_value", "library_q_value")]
#> [1] "PG_Qvalue"        "PG_LibraryQvalue"

$fields() lists every cataloged field of the version as a table; each entry’s id names the software, version, level and slot where the field lives:

spectronaut$fields()[, c("key", "entry_id")]
#>               key                                              entry_id
#> 1             pep         Spectronaut/*/peptidoform_ion/layers/EG_PEP/-
#> 2         q_value      Spectronaut/*/peptidoform_ion/layers/EG_Qvalue/-
#> 3 library_q_value Spectronaut/21/peptidoform_ion/var/-/EG_LibraryQvalue
#> 4         q_value    Spectronaut/21/protein/layers/PG_QValue_Run_Wise/-
#> 5         q_value                Spectronaut/21/protein/var/-/PG_Qvalue
#> 6 library_q_value         Spectronaut/21/protein/var/-/PG_LibraryQvalue

The data of a result
read_parsed_levels() reads a result apb2 wrote, .parquet, .h5ad or .duckdb, into ParsedLevels, one anndataR AnnData per level. The test bundle carries synthetic Parquet results; this one has MaxQuant’s peptidoform-ion level.

results <- tempfile()
archive <- system.file(
    "extdata", "test-bundle", "results.tar.gz",
    package = "apbCatalogR"
)
utils::untar(archive, exdir = results)
result <- read_parsed_levels(
    file.path(results, "maxquant_wide-peptidoform_ion.parquet")
)
result
#> <ParsedLevels>
#>   peptidoform_ion: 2 x 3, layers: Intensity, MS_MS_count, Retention_time, Retention_length, Calibrated_retention_time, Calibrated_retention_time_start, Calibrated_retention_time_finish, Score, PEP
result$levels$peptidoform_ion
#> InMemoryAnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 2 × 3
#>     obs: 'Raw_file', 'Experiment', 'Fraction'
#>     var: 'ProForma_ion', 'Sequence', 'Modified_sequence', 'Modifications', 'Charge', 'Mass', 'Proteins', 'Leading_proteins', 'Leading_razor_protein', 'protein_Protein_IDs', 'Protein_IDs', 'ProForma_peptidoform', 'ProForma_peptide', 'Reverse', 'Potential_contaminant', 'apb_Decoy', 'apb_Contaminant'
#>     uns: 'apb'
#>     layers: 'MS_MS_count', 'Retention_time', 'Retention_length', 'Calibrated_retention_time', 'Calibrated_retention_time_start', 'Calibrated_retention_time_finish', 'Score', 'PEP'

DataCatalog answers on the result and hands back the data. It composes the named sets alone: apb_alpha, APB’s own fields, answers only when named.

confidence <- DataCatalog$new(result, "confidence_alpha", "apb_alpha")
pep <- confidence$levels$peptidoform_ion$layers[["pep"]]
dim(pep)
#> [1] 2 3

$fields() lists the cataloged fields the result holds, from both sets:

confidence$fields()[, c("set", "slot", "name", "key", "present")]
#>                set   slot                 name                key present
#> 1 confidence_alpha layers                  PEP                pep    TRUE
#> 2        apb_alpha    var     ProForma_peptide            peptide    TRUE
#> 3        apb_alpha    var ProForma_peptidoform        peptidoform    TRUE
#> 4        apb_alpha    var         ProForma_ion    peptidoform_ion    TRUE
#> 5        apb_alpha    var            apb_Decoy              decoy    TRUE
#> 6        apb_alpha    var      apb_Contaminant        contaminant    TRUE
#> 7        apb_alpha    var          Protein_IDs protein_assignment    TRUE
#> 8        apb_alpha    var             Proteins   fasta_accessions    TRUE

Each level of the catalog has anndataR’s slots. A name is read as a key first, then as the level’s own layer or column, as the Python package cf_xarray finds an xarray variable by its CF-convention standard name first. ?Level and ?Slot list the methods:

ion <- confidence$levels$peptidoform_ion
dim(ion$layers[["pep"]])            # a matrix, runs x features
#> [1] 2 3
ion$layers$keys()                   # a character vector
#> [1] "pep"
head(ion$var[["peptidoform_ion"]])  # a vector, one value per feature
#> [1] "F0" "F1" "F2"

The slots read the anndataR AnnData of the level, so a key gives the same data as the vendor’s name in anndataR. A vendor’s own name still reads, and [ gives a data frame, as on anndataR’s obs and var:

# The anndataR AnnData of the level
adata <- result$levels$peptidoform_ion
identical(ion$layers[["pep"]], adata$layers[["PEP"]])
#> [1] TRUE
identical(ion$X, adata$X)
#> [1] TRUE
ion$obs_names
#> [1] "S0" "S1"
ion$var_names
#> [1] "F0" "F1" "F2"
# MaxQuant's own layer, as adata$layers[["Score"]]
ion$layers[["Score"]]
#>     F0  F1  F2
#> S0 0.8 0.9 1.0
#> S1 0.9 1.0 1.1
# A data frame, as adata$obs[c("Raw_file", "Experiment")]
ion$obs[c("Raw_file", "Experiment")]
#>   Raw_file Experiment
#> 1       S0         v0
#> 2       S1         v1
# Keys, each column named as the result names it
ion$var[c("peptidoform_ion", "decoy", "contaminant")]
#>   ProForma_ion apb_Decoy apb_Contaminant
#> 1           F0      TRUE            TRUE
#> 2           F1     FALSE           FALSE
#> 3           F2      TRUE            TRUE

A vendor may name a column as a key is named, as Sage names its quantification q-value q_value. A prefix makes the lookup exact: a set’s prefix asks that set alone and never the level’s own field, v: the level’s own field alone and never the catalog. sets() lists each set’s prefix:

ion$layers$name("c:pep")    # the confidence set alone
#> [1] "PEP"
ion$layers$name("v:Score")  # MaxQuant's own layer alone
#> [1] "Score"
sets()[, c("set", "prefix")]
#>                            set prefix
#> 1              abundance_alpha      a
#> 2             confidence_alpha      c
#> 3 proteobench_entrapment_alpha    pbe
#> 4                    apb_alpha    apb
#> 5         obs_annotation_alpha  annot
#> 6         fasta_peptides_alpha   fpep
#> 7         fasta_proteins_alpha  fprot
#> 8         chromatography_alpha     rt

MaxQuant reports no q-value on this level, so $get() gives NULL, where [[ signals an error; $name() names the field a key reads:

ion$layers$get("q_value")
#> NULL
ion$layers$name("pep")
#> [1] "PEP"

A lookup the catalog cannot answer with one field signals UnresolvedField rather than choosing silently. Spectronaut does not document how its protein quantity combines the precursors, so asking for a summed one is unknown there:

spectronaut <- Catalog$new("Spectronaut", "21.0", "abundance_alpha")
tryCatch(
    spectronaut$levels$protein$layers$get(
        "intensity_norm_settings",
        aggregation = "sum"
    ),
    UnresolvedField = function(condition) conditionMessage(condition)
)
#> [1] "intensity_norm_settings (kind=intensity, normalization=run_setting, aggregation=sum) on protein is unknown: PG_Quantity leaves aggregation unknown; candidates: PG_Quantity"

The same code for every software
The same lookup reads each software’s field; the test bundle holds results of many:

files <- c(
    MaxQuant = "maxquant_wide-peptidoform_ion.parquet",
    Spectronaut = "spectronaut_v21-peptidoform_ion.parquet",
    `DIA-NN` = "diann_v2-peptidoform_ion.parquet"
)
pep_field <- function(file) {
    vendor <- read_parsed_levels(file.path(results, file))
    catalog <- DataCatalog$new(vendor, "confidence_alpha")
    catalog$levels$peptidoform_ion$layers$name("pep")
}
vapply(files, pep_field, character(1))
#>    MaxQuant Spectronaut      DIA-NN 
#>       "PEP"    "EG_PEP"       "PEP"

A protein level reads the same way; DIA-NN’s MaxLFQ intensity, normalized as the run’s settings chose, is the key intensity_norm_settings:

diann <- read_parsed_levels(file.path(results, "diann_v2-protein.parquet"))
protein <- DataCatalog$new(diann, "abundance_alpha")$levels$protein
protein$layers$keys()
#> [1] "intensity_norm_settings"
protein$layers$name("intensity_norm_settings")
#> [1] "PG_MaxLFQ"
protein$layers[["intensity_norm_settings"]]
#>     F0  F1  F2
#> S0 0.0 0.1 0.2
#> S1 0.1 0.2 0.3

Several sets and qualifiers
DataCatalog$new() composes several sets on one result. A key may leave a qualifier open, such as the unit of a retention time; $get() and $name() narrow it, and a lookup no field answers gives NULL:

both <- DataCatalog$new(result, "confidence_alpha", "chromatography_alpha")
both
#> <DataCatalog confidence_alpha, chromatography_alpha: peptidoform_ion>
rt <- both$levels$peptidoform_ion
rt$layers$keys()
#> [1] "aligned_peak_end"       "aligned_peak_start"     "aligned_retention_time"
#> [4] "peak_width"             "pep"                    "retention_time"
rt$layers$name("retention_time", unit = "minute")
#> [1] "Retention_time"
rt$layers$get("retention_time", unit = "second")
#> NULL

Sets an app or an annotation answers
A set of an app’s fields answers once the app has run, and the sample annotation once apb2 annotate has attached it. Opening such a set on a result that lacks them is an error that says what to run:

tryCatch(
    DataCatalog$new(result, "fasta_peptides_alpha"),
    error = function(condition) conditionMessage(condition)
)
#> [1] "fasta_peptides_alpha: apb-fasta has not run on this result; run `apb-fasta verify-peptides`"

DataCatalog$answering_sets() lists the sets a result opens, without an error, so a consumer can leave out the fields of an app that has not run:

DataCatalog$answering_sets(result)
#> [1] "abundance_alpha"              "confidence_alpha"            
#> [3] "proteobench_entrapment_alpha" "apb_alpha"                   
#> [5] "chromatography_alpha"

Requirements
A set may require or recommend fields. enforce checks them once, when the catalog opens: "required" signals one MissingRequiredField listing every missing required field and warns about missing recommended ones; "recommended" signals for both. MaxQuant’s peptidoform level lacks a recommended field of apb_alpha:

peptidoform <- read_parsed_levels(
    file.path(results, "maxquant_wide-peptidoform.parquet")
)
tryCatch(
    DataCatalog$new(peptidoform, "apb_alpha", enforce = "recommended"),
    MissingRequiredField = function(condition) conditionMessage(condition)
)
#> [1] "recommended field peptidoform (kind=peptidoform) on peptidoform is missing: no reviewed MaxQuant ^(1\\.5|1\\.6|2\\.) entry on peptidoform matches"

Rule coverage
rule_coverage() checks every rule against one set; a set with requirements judges each level:

coverage <- rule_coverage("abundance_alpha")
unique(coverage[, c("software", "version", "level", "verdict")])[1:5, ]
#>    software version           level verdict
#> 1  AlphaDIA    1.10 peptidoform_ion    warn
#> 3  AlphaDIA    1.12 peptidoform_ion    warn
#> 5  AlphaDIA     2.x peptidoform_ion    warn
#> 7  AlphaDIA     2.x         protein    <NA>
#> 8 AlphaPept     0.5 peptidoform_ion    pass

A newer catalog
update_catalog() installs a bundle archive into the user cache; later sessions use the newest bundle, shipped or installed. apb-catalog’s make bundle writes the archive. Nothing is downloaded.

update_catalog("apb-catalog/build/apb-catalog-bundle.tar.gz")

Session information

title: apbCatalogR
text:
DOI


apb-catalog’s API in R: look up the fields of an APB result by meaning, such as a PEP or an unnormalized intensity, without naming vendor columns.

New API. This package is new, and its API may still change between releases. Feedback is very welcome: open an issue with what you need, what surprised you, or what broke.

Documentation: anndata-omics-bridge.github.io/apbCatalogR, with the vignette as the walkthrough.
Catalog viewer: fgcz-ms.uzh.ch/public/apb-catalog, every set with its entries, requirements and coverage, in the browser.
Contributing: the sets can be extended to suit your application, and you are welcome to create your own; see Contributing.

The AnnData Proteomics Bridge, apb2, converts the reports of proteomics quantification software into one result layout. Declarative parse rules describe each vendor table, so one parser reads them all.

Software: AlphaDIA, DIA-NN, FragPipe, MaxQuant, PEAKS, Sage, Spectronaut and more

Set
Fields

confidence_alpha
PEP and q-values per run and per feature


proteobench_entrapment_alpha
Precursor q-values for ProteoBench’s entrapment scoring

Answers




Catalog$new(software, software_version, set_name)
From the catalog alone, without data


DataCatalog$new(result, set)
On one result, the named sets alone, and returns the data

The level’s per-sample columns, read with [[ or [.

text:
Reads a result apb2 wrote into a ParsedLevels object, one anndataR AnnData per level, the same for every format: a .h5ad file, a .duckdb file, or the directory apb2 writes for a .parquet result. Reading Parquet needs the arrow package, DuckDB the duckdb and DBI packages, .h5ad the rhdf5 package, with which anndataR reads it.

read_parsed_levels(path)




path


The result, such as converted.h5ad, converted.duckdb or the directory converted.parquet.


A ParsedLevels object.

apb2’s convert command writes the result; each format records its format name and version, and a result of another format or version is refused:


Parquet: a directory ending in .parquet whose manifest.json (format apb2-parsed-levels-parquet, version 9) names every level and table. Each level is a folder under levels/ with obs.parquet, var.parquet, one file per layer in layers/ (features by observations) and the tables of obsm/, varm/, obsp/ and varp/. The result’s own tables are in annotation_tables/ and feature_relations/.


DuckDB: one .duckdb file (format apb2-parsed-levels-duckdb, version 8) holding the same manifest in the table apb2_result_metadata; each table the manifest names is a database table.


h5ad: one .h5ad file of a one-level result in anndata’s layout (format apb2-parsed-levels, version 8), with apb2’s storage descriptor in uns$apb. An .h5ad file other software wrote has none and is refused.
